about.title: Duarte Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A fall on someone else's property can happen fast — a wet floor near a Buena Vista Street storefront, uneven pavement outside an apartment complex, or a poorly lit stairwell in a strip mall off Huntington Drive. In Duarte, these incidents often go unreported at first, and by the time medical bills arrive, the property owner's insurer is already building a defense. California law requires showing the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard and failed to address it, which makes early documentation critical. LawProactive is not a law firm, but a free connection service that puts injured people in touch with independent attorneys across Los Angeles County. If you were hurt on someone else's property in Duarte, we can help you find an attorney who works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless your case results in a recovery. Reach out and let us do the matching.

items.title: Proving Notice Takes Evidence
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. Photos of the condition, witness names, and incident reports matter from day one.

items.title: Surveillance Footage Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Duarte businesses and apartment complexes overwrite security video within days or weeks, so an attorney can send a preservation letter before footage is lost.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning even if you're found partly responsible for the fall, you may still recover a reduced amount based on the other party's share of fault.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Duarte?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a premises liability lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a government entity, such as a public building near Huntington Drive, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim. An attorney can confirm which timeline applies to your situation.

items.question: What if I fell at a store or apartment complex and no one wrote up a report?
items.answer: A missing incident report doesn't end your claim, but it does make documentation more important. Take photos of the hazard, get contact information from anyone who saw it happen, and seek medical care promptly. An attorney can still help gather evidence like maintenance logs or surveillance footage even without a formal report.

items.question: Does it matter that my fall happened near a busy corridor like I-210 or Buena Vista Street?
items.answer: Not directly — premises liability claims focus on the property where you fell, not nearby traffic patterns. That said, properties along high-traffic corridors sometimes see more foot traffic and turnover, which can be relevant to how quickly a hazard should have been noticed and fixed.
